Require substantial continuation outside any crib or parameter-fitting prefix; compare the entire selected search against controls. A short plausible word or thematic resemblance is not a successful decoding.

proposals.title: LP2-15 prime-spiral gaps modulo 28
proposals.input: The supplied 4x4 prime array, related to the known LP2-15 square construction; distinguish this derived array from the printed manuscript cells.
proposals.transform: Traverse the shown spiral in ascending prime order, subtract each predecessor, then reduce each difference modulo 28.
proposals.intake_check: The 15 displayed differences and all 15 residues were independently recomputed and match the screenshots. This is intake arithmetic only, not a completed cycle or decryption experiment.
proposals.criterion: Specify the exact sequence extension and cycle criterion before further inspection. Check recurrence on unseen terms and compare the entire chosen pattern search with appropriate controls. Any proposed rune decoding needs a fixed alphabet, zero-residue treatment, direction, target text, alignment and held-out continuation.
proposals.parameters: The supplied spiral, forward consecutive differences and modulus 28 are fixed. Reversal, alternative paths, gap definitions, other moduli and guessed text mappings are separate choices requiring finite bounds.
missing: An exact definition of the claimed repetitive cycle and where it begins.
A justified extension beyond the 16 supplied primes for an out-of-sample recurrence check.
Why modulus 28 is used and how its residues would map to the 29-rune GP alphabet, if a rune mapping is intended.
A complete decoding rule and fixed target pages if this becomes a cipher proposal.

related_context.role: Known construction of the printed square and its derived Fibonacci-indexed primes.

overlap_notes: Existing records cover related square-derived prime shifts, totient/gap claims and title keys; those do not establish that this exact modulo-28 pattern or a decoding rule has been tested.
Do not count the 15 differences as separate ideas or label a short tail a demonstrated periodic cycle.
proposals.intake_decision: One grouped queued proposal. Preserve the exact supplied data and check overlap before extending existing work or creating a new experiment.
proposals.modulus_review: No rationale for modulus 28 was supplied. GP29 has 29 symbols indexed 0 through 28; index range alone does not justify reduction modulo 28. Modulus 28 can arise for exponents in the nonzero multiplicative group modulo 29, but no such exponent rule was proposed here. Do not invent that motivation or treat a selected residue pattern as cipher evidence.

completed_check.finding: All supplied arithmetic matches; exact fixed period-four continuation fails at the first new gap (4 instead of 8), with 0/8 matching continuation positions.
completed_check.limits: Only this fixed arithmetic continuation; no rune decoder supplied or tested.

queue_review.covered_exact_scope: Published record verifies source 16 Fibonacci-indexed primes/15 gaps; fixed 8,20,10,6 tail occurs once and eight new terms break period-four continuation.
queue_review.untested_or_undefined_remainder: A further rune mapping or a different claimed cycle would need an exact rule and holdout criterion.
queue_review.readiness: No remaining arithmetic check for this stated cycle.
